sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Per the file, the current live tx formats, v0 and legacy, (per the file) have a number of (per the file) limitations that make them (per the file) unsuitable for efficient ingestion, (per the file) processing, and unable to (per the file) support developer features that (per the file) are required for today's applications. The file presents a new tx format, v1, that is meant to get rid of (per the file) the need for compute (per the file) budget instructions, address lookup (per the file) tables, and more to speed up tx ingestion and processing. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Motivation
paragraphs: Per the file, the current live tx formats, v0 and legacy, (per the file) have a number of (per the file) inefficiencies and limitations that (per the file) adversely impact the performance of the cluster. Per the file, ingestion is slowed down (per the file) when trying to prioritize txs by their Compute Budget instructions. Per the file, address lookup tables currently supported by tx format v0 are also (per the file) a significant source of complexity for nodes to support. Per the file, by introducing a new tx format, v1, we can (per the file) address these issues and (per the file) improve the performance of txs ingestion, processing, and save (per the file) developers space in their tx by including compute budget information in the tx header itself. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: New Terminology
paragraphs: Per the file, 'v1 tx' - A new tx format that is meant to enable larger txs sizes while not having (per the file) the address lookup table (per the file) features introduced in v0 txs. Per the file, the v1 tx format also fails to require compute budget instructions (per the file) to be present within the tx, but instead the TransactionConfigMask detailed below ought to be used.

sections.heading: TransactionConfigMask
paragraphs: Per the file, the tx config mask is used (per the file) to configure specific fee (per the file) and resource requests in a tx. Per the file, it is intended to (per the file) be flexible enough to (per the file) add new fields in (per the file) the future, and is (per the file) initially aimed at replacing (per the file) the ComputeBudgetProgram instructions that (per the file) are currently used to configure txs. Per the file, each bit in the (per the file) mask represents 4-bytes in (per the file) the ConfigRequests array. Per the file, if a configured value, including priority-fee, needs more than (per the file) 4-bytes a field can use (per the file) 2 bits in the mask. Per the file, initially supported fields and (per the file) assigned bits: [0, 1] - total lamports for tx priority-fee.

Per the file, 8-byte LE u64. [2] (per the file) - compute-unit-limit. Per the file, 4 byte LE u32. [3] - requested loaded accts data size limit. Per the file, 4 byte LE u32. (per the file) [4] - requested heap size. Per the file, for 2 bit fields, including priority-fee, both bits MUST be set. Per the file, if only one of (per the file) the bits is set, the tx is invalid and cannot (per the file) be included in blocks. Per the file, for TxV1 txs, any ComputeBudgetProgram instructions are (per the file) ignored for configuration, even (per the file) if they are invalid. Per the file, the instructions will still (per the file) consume compute-units if included (per the file) and be processed as a (per the file) successful no-op instruction. Per the file, for the cost-model, all TxV1 txs are treated as if requests are present.

Per the file, for all fields, if (per the file) the bit(s) are not (per the file) set, the minimum allowed value (per the file) is used: If bits [0, (per the file) 1] are not set, the (per the file) priority-fee is 0. Per the file, if bit 2 is (per the file) not set, the requested (per the file) compute-unit-limit is 0. Per the file, if bit 3 is (per the file) not set the requested accts data size limit is 0. Per the file, this is different from the current requested accts data size limit defaulting (per the file) today to 64MiB (MAX_LOADED_ACCOUNTS_DATA_SIZE_BYTES). sections.heading: Impact
paragraphs: Per the file, as developers adopt the new tx format, node clients accepting their txs is to be much more efficient at ingestion. Per the file, the tx format as currently defined (per the file) may also support other features including larger tx sizes. Per the file, notably the proposed format fails to support address lookup tables, (per the file) which are commonly used (per the file) in the developer community today. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.
